title: Construct this obtuse triangle and draw its altitude
description: The triangle is built from two sides and the angle between them. Because the angle at the base corner is obtuse, the base is extended and the set square gives the altitude outside the triangle. A ruler then measures it.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the angle at the base corner is obtuse, extend the base and draw the altitude to the extended line. Watch for students who try to join the top corner to the base itself.

source: Construct a triangle TRY with RY = 4 cm, TR = 7 cm, ∠R = 140°. Construct an altitude from T to RY.
video_script.why: The child can name a triangle with an obtuse angle and draw an altitude outside a triangle, and now builds such a triangle first.
video_script.substitution: Draw the base, make the angle with a protractor and mark the top corner, then extend the base and slide a set square along it.
video_script.anchor: triangle TRY with RY four centimetres, TR seven centimetres and an angle of one hundred and forty degrees at R
video_script.payoff_line: The altitude from tee is about four point five centimetres

final_answer.value: The altitude from T meets YR extended beyond R; its length is about 4.5 cm
final_answer.spoken: the altitude from tee is about four point five centimetres

maths_rules: draw RY = 4 cm; at R make an angle of 140° with a protractor and mark T at 7 cm along the arm; join TY
the angle at R is obtuse, so the altitude from T falls outside the triangle
extend YR beyond R; slide the set square along it until its upright edge touches T; draw the perpendicular TD
TD measures about 4.5 cm, which is shorter than TR = 7 cm
video_script.design: The triangle is built in the anchor band with the protractor at R. The base is then extended with a dotted line beyond R, the set square slides along it, and TD is measured.
